summary: Lookout on Allard Mountain with a view of the Kalum Lake area; George Dupont staffed it in August 1966 per a Terrace newspaper report. Build date and fate not found.

events.note: George Dupont was the lookout in August 1966, per the Terrace "Omineca" Herald report quoted by Canada Lookouts

evidence.supports: Lookout is on a knoll that is part of Allard Mountain
evidence.quote: Beaver Bluff is on a knoll which is part of Allard Mountain.

evidence.supports: Location in the Kitimat-Stikine area (page heading)
Lookout building about 3,000 feet above the valley (about 914 m)
evidence.quote: The lookout building is about 3,000 feet above the valley

evidence.supports: Date of the report and newspaper source
George Dupont kept watch and had a commanding view of the Kalum Lake area
evidence.quote: George Dupont has a commanding view of the entire Kalum Lake area

evidence.supports: Lookout equipment: two-way radio, 60-power telescope, three sets of binoculars
evidence.quote: His lookout is equipped with a 2-way radio, a 60 power telescope and three sets of binoculars.

evidence.supports: Smoke reports taken by range reading and relayed to Terrace Fire Control Centre
evidence.quote: When he spots smoke he immediately takes a range reading and relays the information to Terrace Fire Control Centre.

evidence.supports: Main food supply airlifted in by helicopter
evidence.quote: Most of the year's main food supply is airlifted in by helicopter

evidence.supports: Occasional trips to Terrace for fresh meat and produce
evidence.quote: George picks up fresh meat and produce on his occasional trips to Terrace.

sources.title: Beaver Bluff (quoting the Terrace "Omineca" Herald, 3 August 1966)

notes_for_editor: Single secondhand source: a Canada Lookouts page quoting the 1966 Terrace Herald. It gives no build date, no fate and no site description today. The page gives longitude as 128.883 with no minus sign; the record's -128.883 is correct for BC. Two Facebook group posts (https://www.facebook.com/groups/bcforestfirelookouts/posts/26262324176789501/ and https://www.facebook.com/groups/bcforestfirelookouts/posts/7662256627222871/) describe the tower as abandoned, last used per the log book in 2006, but their text is not readable through fetch_text, so no fate is stated. Check them by hand before adding abandoned or other fate events. The page prints the elevation as 907 with no unit; the record's 907 m assumes metres.
